actions.reason: Inspect visible workspace to locate any launch scripts or relevant files for starting the ISO in QEMU
Define the task-specific success criteria from the visible request before making changes

args.objective: Start /app/alpine.iso in QEMU in the background so telnet 127.0.0.1 6665 reaches the Alpine login prompt and remains available.
required_artifacts: A reachable telnet service on 127.0.0.1:6665 that presents the Alpine login prompt
required_behaviors: QEMU must be started in the background and left running
Connecting with telnet to 127.0.0.1 6665 must show the login prompt
known_invalid_patterns: Only proving the ISO file exists
Only proving QEMU starts without confirming the telnet prompt
Only checking that port 6665 is open without verifying the login prompt
verification_plan: Inspect the workspace for existing boot assets and any helper scripts
Start QEMU with host port forwarding to expose guest telnet on 127.0.0.1:6665
Probe the port and confirm the login prompt appears
finalization_evidence_required: Receipt-backed evidence of the QEMU launch command and background process
Receipt-backed evidence from a telnet/probe showing the Alpine login prompt on 127.0.0.1:6665

actions.reason: Track the multi-step service bring-up and verification workflow

args.objective: Bring up Alpine ISO in QEMU and expose login prompt on localhost:6665
args.current_focus: Inspect workspace contents and determine the correct QEMU invocation
implementation_approach: Look for existing disk/ISO assets and any helper launch scripts
Use QEMU user networking with hostfwd to guest telnet port 23 on host port 6665
Run QEMU detached/backgrounded and capture logs
Probe localhost:6665 until the login prompt is observed
validation_strategy: Use a telnet or netcat probe against 127.0.0.1:6665
Confirm the prompt text matches Alpine login prompt behavior
Keep the VM running after successful probe
known_bad_behavior: Port open but no login prompt
evidence_gaps: Need to inspect visible files and any existing receipts before launching
risks: QEMU may not be installed or may require a specific machine/acceleration setting
The ISO may need a bootable disk or different serial console settings
next_steps: Determine available QEMU binary and launch options
Start VM and probe telnet endpoint
